body.statement:
For a bivariate Poisson CPCM \(X\to Y\) with \(Y\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda(x))\), the direction is not identifiable exactly in the exceptional case
\[
\lambda(x)=\exp(ax+b),\qquad
\Pr(X=x)\ \mathrel{\propto}\ \frac{\exp\{\lambda(x)+cx\}}{x!},
\qquad x\in\mathbb N _0,
\]
for constants \(a<0\) and \(b,c\in\mathbb R\).

source.locator: Consequence 6, first bullet, printed page 8; proof in Appendix C.2, printed pages 41--42
source.verbatim_statement: The causal graph is not identifiable iff λ(x)=exp(ax+b) and P(X₁=x) ∝ exp(λ(x)+cx)/x!, for a<0 and b,c∈ℝ.
